Scene Director **3.9.0** brings Prompt Studio and LoRA Dataset to **macOS Apple Silicon**, **macOS Intel**, **Windows x64** and **Linux x64**.

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Apple Silicon, macOS 13+ | `scene-director-3.9.0-macos-arm64.zip` |
| Intel, macOS 13+ | `scene-director-3.9.0-macos-x64.zip` |
| Windows x64 | `scene-director-3.9.0-windows-x64.zip` |
| Linux x64 | `scene-director-3.9.0-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

Both Mac apps are Developer ID signed, Apple-notarized and include a stapled ticket. On Mac, extract and move **Scene Director.app** to Applications. On Windows, extract the entire ZIP and open **Scene Director.exe**. On Linux, extract the archive and run `./scene-director` inside its **Scene Director** folder. Python is included. Windows and Linux downloads are not code-signed. Linux is built on Ubuntu 22.04 and requires a desktop with GTK 3, NSS, GBM and ALSA libraries.

Homebrew selects the native Mac build:

```sh
brew install --cask cyberdeliaAI/apps/scene-director
```

Quit the app before replacing an older version. Settings, prompts and saved dataset sessions are stored separately and are retained.

Included: the proportional window layout from beta.2; separate creative/precise sampling; prompt actions, favorites, History and saved briefs; rotating choices and ComfyUI queuing; dataset crop ratios, buckets, zoom/pan, auto crop, caption scripts, parallel captioning, review and training exports. Review fixes preserve multiline prompts and slot choices, and Stop cancels connected vision requests while rejecting late results.

Each native build is checked on its matching runner, then extracted and checked again for architecture, frozen-service operation, real interface startup, renderer isolation, clean shutdown, licenses and portable HTTPS roots. Mac builds also pass nested signature, hardened runtime, stapled-ticket and Gatekeeper checks. `SHA256SUMS` verifies downloads; the individual `.verification.json` files and combined `verification.json` record the source revision and completed checks.

A compatible model server is required; Vision workflows need a vision-capable model. Live model quality, real ComfyUI workflows, other Linux distributions and older supported macOS versions have not been evaluated by the release checks.
